newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo expects to sell JCI stake soon.
newsitem.headline: Anglo expects to sell JCI stake soon.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it expected talks on the sale of its majority shareholding in JCI Ltd to kick off soon.

Anglo spokesman Michael Spicer told Reuters the sale of 35 percent of Anglo's 47 percent stake in JCI would become a priority after the conclusion of the recent sale of the 35 percent controlling interest in conglomerate Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) to black businesses.
"It is absolutely in everyone's interest to move quickly. We anticipate moving more quickly," Spicer said.
JCI is South Africa's sixth-largest mining company and Anglo has said it wants to sell the company to black interests.
Analysts expect the sale of the JCI stake to be similiar to the Johnnic deal, when 23 black business groups came up with 2.7 billion rand to buy control of Johnnic.
The deal gives blacks control or influence over companies representing nearly a tenth of the capitalisation of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Spicer said with the Johnnic deal paving the way for black empowerment groups to acquire pieces of corporate South Africa, Anglo believed talks on the sale could start as early as next month.
"I truly believe that as soon as we've put the other one (Johnnic) to bed, and we are right on the end of the month now when it will happen, we will start moving," Spicer said.

On Wednesday, Business Day newspaper quoted Don Ncube, chairman of black empowerment group Real African Investments Ltd (Rail), as saying the company had decided not to pursue a deal with Anglo to buy the JCI stake.
The withdrawal of Rail leaves the way open for rivals New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail), Capital Alliance and African Renaissance to make their bids for JCI.

Business Day quoted Nail sources as saying the group, whose chief negotiator Cyril Ramaphosa is expected to take up the chairmanship of Johnnic, would consider buying the entire 35 percent stake for sale by Anglo but the company would not rule out forming a partnership with other black empowerment groups.
Johannesburg investment analyst John Clemmow said Ramaphosa had his eyes set on acquiring JCI for Nail.
"Cyril clearly wants to be chairman of JCI more than he wants to chairman of Johnnic," Clemmow said.
Clemmow said JCI management was frustrated at the pace of the sale because the company had clear ideas on restructuring and the future direction of JCI.
"Within JCI they have very clear plans on restructuring and doing lots of things.
"If you talk to people in JCI they will come out as being frustrated in as far as they are not able to do these things while the sale is going on," he added.
